test_title: SSC CHSL Tier-II Exam 2024 Official Paper (Held On: 18 Nov, 2024).
subject: general
question: Which of the following best describes the primary difference between broadband and dial-up Internet connections?

options.text: Dial-up uses a telephone line, while broadband uses various technologies for higher speeds.
Broadband is only available in urban areas, while dial-up is available everywhere.
Dial-up requires a cable connection, while broadband does not.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Dial-up uses a telephone line, while broadband uses various technologies for higher speeds.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__

• **Dial-up Internet** requires a telephone line for connectivity. Users connect to the Internet by dialing a phone number, which establishes a connection to their Internet Service Provider (ISP).

• **Broadband Internet** utilizes a variety of technologies, such as DSL, cable, fiber optics, and satellite, to provide much higher speeds compared to dial-up.

• Broadband connections are **always on** and do not require the user to dial in each time they want to access the Internet.

• Broadband can handle more data and allows for simultaneous use of Internet and telephone services without interference.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Dial-up Internet**

• Dial-up Internet access is a form of Internet access that uses the facilities of the public switched telephone network (PSTN) to establish a dialed connection to an Internet service provider (ISP).

• Users must dial a phone number to connect to their ISP's server, which can be time-consuming.

• Dial-up typically offers speeds of up to 56 kbps, which is significantly slower than broadband.

• One of the major disadvantages is that it ties up the phone line, preventing incoming and outgoing calls while connected to the Internet.

• **Broadband Internet**

• Broadband is a high-speed Internet connection that is always on and faster than the traditional dial-up access.

• It includes several types of high-speed transmission technologies such as Digital Subscriber Line (DSL), cable modem, fiber, wireless, satellite, and broadband over powerlines (BPL).

• Speeds can vary significantly, with broadband typically providing speeds from 25 Mbps to 1 Gbps.

• Broadband connections allow for simultaneous use of telephone and Internet services, making it more versatile and efficient.
